stem:
Butanedioic acid can be made in a three-step synthesis using ethane as the starting material.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the reagents and conditions needed for step 1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Name the other product also formed in step 1 which is an isomer of $\mathbf{A}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: State the reagents and conditions needed for step 2.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Butanedioic acid cannot be oxidised by a warm, aqueous solution of any commonly used oxidising agents but ethanedioic acid can.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Identify the oxidising agent that could be used to oxidise ethanedioic acid.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: State the product(s) of the reaction in $\mathbf{(e)(i)}$.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: Compare and explain the relative acidities of hexanoic acid, hexan-1-ol and phenol.

parts.label: (g)
(g)(i)
parts.text: Identify the protons in the methylpropanedioic acid molecule that are responsible for each area of the proton NMR spectrum.

parts.label: (g)(ii)
parts.text: Name the splitting pattern shown at $\delta$ 3.3 and explain how it arises.

parts.label: (g)(iii)
parts.text:
The carbon-13 NMR spectra of butanedioic acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and methylpropanedioic acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH(CH}_3\text{)CO}_2\text{H}$ are different.

State the number of peaks

- in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of butanedioic acid

- in the carbon-13 NMR spectrum of methylpropanedioic acid.
